_comment: WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Before it, each blueprint invented its own symptom words. There were
24 words across 11 blueprints and 22 of them were used by exactly one blueprint. So picking
a blueprint by matching words would have scored near-perfect - not because selection works,
but because each word named its own answer. Any selection number built on that is worthless.
The rule now: a blueprint may only use words from this file. It may not add a private one.
Blueprints that look alike are then forced to share words, and selection has to do real work.
The words are grouped on axes (scope, errors, latency, throughput, resource, network).
Grouping is deliberate: two different faults that both slow one service must both say
scope.single_component, and something else has to tell them apart.
STATUS: PROPOSED, NOT MEASURED. The words were derived by reading the 11 existing blueprints.
Which words are actually TRUE for each fault family has not been measured yet. That needs
running the survey over the labelled packs. Until then no blueprint's symptom list is evidence.
`measured_by` names the capability that decides the word. Words with capability null are not
yet measurable and must not be used in selection.

scope.what: How much of the system is affected, and in what shape.
scope.note: Exactly one scope word should be true per incident.

scope.single_component.what: One service or container is slow. The rest are fine.

scope.several_components.what: Several services degrade at the same time, but not all.

scope.host_wide.what: Everything on the host degrades together.

scope.along_a_path.what: The slowdown follows a caller-callee path, not one component.

errors.what: Are requests failing, or only slow?

errors.none.what: Requests succeed. They are only slower.

errors.partial.what: Some requests fail while others succeed, at the same time.

errors.on_connect.what: Failures happen when opening a connection, not when serving.

latency.what: The shape of the slowdown, not its size.

latency.raised_steadily.what: Latency is higher and stays higher.

latency.erratic.what: Latency jumps around. Some requests normal, some far worse.

latency.connection_setup_slow.what: The delay is before the request starts, at connect time.

throughput.what: Is the system doing more work or less?

throughput.down.what: Fewer requests are completing than in the baseline.

throughput.unchanged.what: Work rate is the same. Only latency moved.

resource.what: What is being consumed, and is anything at its ceiling?

resource.host_cpu_saturated.what: Host CPU is at or near the ceiling across all cores.

resource.cpu_busy_not_saturated.what: CPU is clearly busier than baseline but not at the ceiling.

resource.cpu_low_while_slow.what: The system is slow while CPU use is low or falling.

resource.disk_busy.what: Disk request rate or service time is well above baseline.

resource.descriptors_exhausted.what: Opening a file or socket fails because the limit is reached.

resource.process_churn.what: Processes are being created far faster than baseline.

resource.none_saturated.what: Nothing is near a ceiling, yet the system is slow.

waiting.what: What threads are waiting on. This is what kernel traces see and metrics do not.

waiting.runqueue.what: Threads are runnable but not getting a CPU.

waiting.in_syscall.what: Threads are blocked inside a syscall, waiting on something else.

waiting.on_lock.what: Threads are parked on a user-level lock.

suspect.resource_quiet.what: The component everything waits on is itself using no resources.

network.what: Network health and volume, kept apart on purpose.
network.note: Impairment and volume are different questions. A busy healthy link is not a broken one.

network.loss_present.what: Packets are retransmitted or dropped in the queue.

network.loss_absent.what: No meaningful retransmission or queue drop.

network.outbound_volume_high.what: Sustained outbound bytes well above baseline.

network.name_resolution_slow.what: Name lookups take far longer than baseline.

rules: A blueprint may only use words defined here.
A word used by exactly one blueprint is a warning. It may be naming its own answer.
A blueprint must declare at least one word that another blueprint also declares.
Words with measured_by null may not be used for selection.
Adding a word requires showing two faults that the existing words cannot tell apart.
